response.sql: WITH item_stats AS (SELECT p.product_id, pc.product_type_description AS ptd, AVG(CAST(oi.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty, COUNT(*) AS item_cnt FROM Order_Items oi JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN Product_Categories pc ON pc.production_type_code = p.production_type_code GROUP BY p.product_id, pc.product_type_description), shares AS (SELECT ptd, avg_qty, item_cnt, item_cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(item_cnt) FROM item_stats) AS share FROM item_stats), per_type AS (SELECT ptd, AVG(avg_qty) AS a_qty, AVG(item_cnt) AS a_cnt, AVG(share) AS a_share FROM shares GROUP BY ptd) SELECT AVG(a_qty) AS avg_quantity, AVG(a_cnt) AS avg_order_item_count, AVG(a_share) AS avg_share FROM per_type;

assumptions.assumption: product_quantity is stored as text but numeric; it is cast to a number for averaging, and non-numeric/missing values are ignored by AVG (non-numeric text may cast to 0 in SQLite).
Products are grouped into types by product_type_description (not by type code), and every product has a matching category via inner join.
Order items are counted by row count per product (COUNT(*)), including those with a missing quantity.
